source.title: Insights into a radiology-specialised multimodal large language model with sparse autoencoders
source.authors: Kenza Bouzid; Shruthi Bannur; Felix Meissen; Daniel Coelho de Castro; A. Schwaighofer; J. Alvarez-Valle; Stephanie L. Hyland

record.tranche_reason: The paper applies a Matryoshka SAE to discover and steer radiology concepts, and mentions splitting as a possible interpretation of repeated feature descriptions. It does not test how features relate across dictionary sizes, whether their activations partition a parent feature, or the geometric or objective claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports seven instances of apparent repetition among 61 features with detection F1 above 0.85 and says these may indicate composition or splitting. This is included as a result about repeated descriptions, not as a test of any listed version. The SAE-size and sparsity experiments are reported in terms of reconstruction, sparsity, and dead features, not splitting. Steering outcomes concern induced changes to reports and do not test the claim.
record.test_reason: The study applies a Matryoshka SAE to MAIRA-2 for concept discovery and steering. It mentions splitting only as a possible reading of repeated feature descriptions within one SAE. It makes no comparison across dictionary sizes, no activation-coverage or geometry analysis, and no objective comparison bearing on splitting. It therefore does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find a small set of highly interpretable, clinically relevant features (288 of 16,384 have F1 > 0.75). Repeated descriptions among these may reflect feature composition or splitting; this is untested. Steering works with mixed success and mostly produces off-target changes. The authors also speculate that poorly disentangled features (splitting, absorption or composition) may explain the steering failures.
record.recipe_differences: No comparison testing the original dictionary-size method. The study uses a Matryoshka SAE on a radiology-specialised multimodal model.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports experiments over expansion factors and sparsity parameters for reconstruction, sparsity, and dead features, but not their effect on splitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Among 61 features with detection F1 > 0.85, seven instances of apparently repeated descriptions occur within one SAE. For example, f13515 and f13911 are both described as 'Elevation of the hemidiaphragm'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a single Matryoshka SAE on a radiology MLLM, some highly interpretable latents receive near-identical automated descriptions. This may reflect splitting or composition, but the study does not distinguish between them.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Actionable Interpretability (AIW 2025) at ICML, as stated in the paper
record.problems: The repetition result is based on feature descriptions, not a direct comparison of activations or directions across dictionaries. The text also gives inconsistent expansion-factor details: the main methods describe ef=4 as the selected setting, while Table A.2 lists expansion factor 8; it notes that Matryoshka group sizes were accidentally reversed.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results meet the row criteria for the listed versions. SAE reconstruction and sparsity hyperparameter results do not measure splitting; steering results measure induced report changes.

untested.parts: No comparison of features across dictionary sizes. The expansion-factor sweep reports only reconstruction, sparsity and dead features.
There is no test of the splitting pattern in large models or open SAE releases.
There is no test of nested families, geometric closeness, or concept hierarchy.
There is no parent/child activation analysis and no test of absorption across size or sparsity.
There is no cross-size decomposition and no test for novel latents.
Matryoshka is used, but its effect on splitting is not compared against other objectives. The architecture benchmark reports reconstruction only.

record.verdict_notes: The text is inconsistent on configuration: the methods section gives ef=4 (16,384 features), while Table A.2 lists expansion factor 8. The Matryoshka group-size reversal was acknowledged by the authors. The paper cites Bricken et al. and Chanin et al. only in discussion.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of feature identities or activations across dictionary sizes; no test of input coverage or directional proximity.
One radiology-specialised model is studied; there is no test of the splitting pattern across large models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested feature families, geometric closeness, or correspondence to a concept hierarchy.
No test of parent-child activation coverage or whether size or sparsity changes absorption.
No cross-size decomposition into combinations of latents or test for novel latents.
No comparison of SAE objectives for splitting, or test of whether the training objective produces it.

rows.subject: MAIRA-2
rows.operation_detail: Counted instances of apparent repetition in feature descriptions among features with F1 above 0.85.
rows.measure: Instances of apparent repetition in feature descriptions
rows.note: Authors suggest repetition may be evidence of composition or splitting. The result does not establish splitting across dictionary sizes, shared input coverage, or geometric proximity.
rows.check: This counts near-duplicate LLM-generated descriptions within a single SAE dictionary, over a selected subset of 61 features with F1 > 0.85. It does not measure splitting across dictionary sizes, shared input coverage, or directional proximity, so it cannot bear on V1–V6. Note that the Matryoshka group sizes were accidentally reversed (App. A.2).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
